quotes: From the Jan 19 Familygram: "Tuesday, January 16th, was a warm, clear day in San Diego, but a number of eyes were moist as the long blast on JOUETT's whistle signified that she was backing away from pier No. 2... As JOUETT nosed her way out the channel, the pier thronged with families, the city of San Diego, and finally Point Loma disappeared in the mist as we proceeded west to new adventures and service to our country." From Mike's letter, 21 Jan 1968: "I got back to the ship about 5 PM last Tuesday. Bill called us at Georgia Mae's about 10 Monday evening... quotes: From Mike's letter, 21 Jan 1968: "We have a calendar back here in the gun control room that we are keeping track of the days on. We figure the longest the cruise could last is 190 days (July 30). That seems like a long time but some day we will be able to look back on all the days as a lot of new experiences for most of us." [Letter]

Context: On 23 January 1968, USS Pueblo (AGER-2) was seized by North Korean forces in the Sea of Japan. One sailor (Fireman Duane D. Hodges) was killed; the 82 surviving crew were imprisoned and tortured for 11 months. The U.S. Navy responded with Operation Formation Star — the largest naval buildup around the Korean Peninsula since the Korean War — placing enormous strain on the Seventh Fleet just as it would be needed for the Tet Offensive. Jouett was in Pearl Harbor at the time.

From the Feb 18 Familygram: "On January 21, the green mountains of the island of Oahu welcomed us into Pearl Harbor. A visit to this Naval Base is a visit into history... Directly across from our berth stood the impressive Arizona Memorial, built on the sunken battleship, that is still a tomb to a thousand men, and still bleeds oil occasionally into the placid harbor." [Familygram]

Context: The Tet Offensive began on January 30–31, 1968 — the largest coordinated offensive by NVA/Viet Cong forces during the entire war, with simultaneous attacks across South Vietnam. Jouett was still in transit, crossing the Pacific into what would become the most dangerous period of the Vietnam War.

They point out on the map what operations have been taking place and how it involves us... They say that at Khe Sahn there is most likely to be one of the most decisive battles take place soon." [Letter]
From Mike's letter, 12 Mar 1968: "I have held off long enough telling you, but I have grown a mustache. I started it on Jan. 28 and will probably shave it off in Japan." [Letter]

From Mike's letter, 16 Mar 1968: "Today the ship had its 100th helicopter landing... About 1330 we had a fire break out in one of the radar power rooms. They got it put out quick and there was very little damage. It was an electrical fire caused by some overheated wiring. So today has been one of our more eventful days out here." [Letter]

From Mike's letter, 16 Mar 1968: "Every Monday evening at supper they pass out these malaria pills for us to take. They make you feel a little sick the next day but thats better than being laid up in some hospital for a couple of months. I suppose those Marines welcome that because at least they can get away from here without having to take a bullet to do it." [Letter]

From the Mar 18 Familygram: "Not all days, however, are filled with the drama of a SAR incident... Our helicopter, affectionately known as 'Clem II', is readied for immediate launch. As the Officer of the Deck turns the ship into the wind, pilots and flight crew dash to their places in Clem II; the ship's Helo Detail--deck handlers and firefighters--man their stations. Within minutes, Clem II is cleared for take-off and rises into the air." [Familygram]

PATTISON, [32 volunteers] contributed their labor to two small churches in villages near Yokosuka, completely painting one church and the pastor's home." [Familygram]

Context: On 4 April 1968, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee. Jouett was in Yokosuka, Japan. Mike's letter of April 19 notes: "The ships in the fleet flew the flag at half-mast for about five days." [Letter, 19 Apr 1968]

entries: At sea, SAR station. Weather: clear, hot (air 85°, water 79°, wind 5 knots, calm seas, visibility 12 miles). 1300 — SAR ALERT: Aircraft downed 13 NM from Jouett. Location: 32mi 80° from Vinh, 24mi offshore, 15mi SE of Hon Matt Island. BIG MOTHER launched. RECOVERS ONE OF TWO CREW — injured, treated, evacuated to carrier for further aid. Resume search but UNABLE TO FIND OTHER CREW MEMBER. 1400 — USS Buckley (DD-808) boat brings debris and wreckage aboard Jouett. Mike records the aircraft as "A-5" in his logbook — information passed second-hand in the heat of the moment.
quotes: HC-7 Rescue 41 — Official Record: The downed aircraft was F-4J Phantom, BuNo 155554, VF-33 "Tarsiers," call sign "Root Beer-204," from USS America (CVA-66). (The HC-7 record's header says "USS Ranger (CVS-61)," but its own narrative and the Command History place VF-33 on America.) A flight of F-4Js was attacking a road intersection near Don Cay, 15 miles south of Vinh, when LT Eric Parker Brice's aircraft was hit by 37mm AAA at 4,500 feet after dropping Mk82 bombs. Hydraulics failed, controls damaged, throttles stuck at full military power. LT Brice flew the crippled aircraft 25 miles out to sea on rudder alone before the Phantom caught fire. He ordered his NFO to eject, but his own canopy failed to jettison — LT Brice was last seen trying to push the canopy free so his ejection seat could fire. KIA — body not recovered (Vietnam Wall, Panel 60W, Row 008). His NFO, LT William A. Simmons, ejected into the water with a broken left leg, broken right arm, and multiple cuts and bruises. [HC-7 Rescue Log; vietnamairlosses.com]

The Rescue: At 1255, Jouett's 1MC announced SAR alert. Big Mother (SH-3A Sikorsky Seaking, HC-7 Det 110) launched at 1300 — crew: pilot LTJG Richard A. Wiley, co-pilot ENS Byron L. Dieckman, ATN-2 Leonard J. Gonerka, AX-3 James A. Lawrence. Arrived on scene at 1308, vectored to survivor by wingman. Survivor spotted by day smoke at 1309. Swimmer dropped, cleared parachute shroud lines. LT Simmons aboard helicopter at 1312. Big Mother landed on Jouett at 1318 — 23 minutes from alert to survivor on deck. Simmons received emergency medical treatment on the helo deck, then taken to Jouett's sick bay. Photography by Ronald J. Bain, FM-2, USS Jouett. [HC-7 Rescue Log]

Note: The 1968 Command Operations Report identifies this as an "F-4 Phantom from USS AMERICA (CVA66)." Mike's logbook records "A-5 downed." The HC-7 rescue log definitively identifies the aircraft as an F-4J from VF-33, USS Ranger. In the urgency of a SAR alert, details passed over the 1MC and through the crew could easily become garbled — an A-5 Vigilante and F-4 Phantom are both twin-engine, twin-tail carrier jets operating from the same task force. Even the ship's official Command Operations Report got the carrier wrong (America vs. Ranger). [COR, 1 Mar 1969]

Mike's Super 8 film of this rescue — the Big Mother scramble, flight quarters, and recovery — survives as digitized footage: `19680604 - DLG-29 Flight Quarters.mp4`. The weather that day (clear, hot, calm seas, 12-mile visibility) matches the bright, sunny conditions visible in the film. [Video]

The friendly fire incident involving USAF F-4 Phantoms mistakenly attacking HMAS Hobart, USS Boston, and several small craft near Tiger Island on 17 June indicated chaotic air defense conditions in the same area where Jouett was firing Terrier missiles at MIGs that same day. [Jouett Jargon]

At sea, SAR/AAW station. 0022 — SAR ALERT: F-4J Phantom (BuNo 155546, "Root Beer 210") from VF-33 "Tarsiers," USS America, hit by SA-2 missile 20 miles northwest of Vinh. Location: 22mi 210° from Vinh, 7.5mi INLAND. BOTH CREW RESCUED — LCDR John "Claw" Holtzclaw and LCDR John "Zeke" Burns — by "Clementine Two" (UH-2A Seasprite, HC-7 Det 104, based on USS Preble). Crew: LTJG Clyde E. Lassen (pilot), LTJG Clarence L. Cook (copilot), AE-2 Bruce B. Dallas, ADJ-3 Donald West. Harrowing night rescue under heavy enemy fire in total darkness. Multiple landing attempts in rice paddies. Starboard door torn off by gunfire. Helicopter lands on Jouett at ~0240 WITH ONLY 5 MINUTES OF FUEL REMAINING (135 lbs). LTJG CLYDE LASSEN AWARDED THE MEDAL OF HONOR — the only Navy helicopter pilot to receive this honor during the Vietnam War. (USS Lassen, DDG-82, later named for him.) 1615 — GQ, MIGs close to 40 miles.
quotes: Stars & Stripes, 26 June 1968 — "After 2 Hairy Hours, F4 Crew Rescued": "The rescue of a downed fighter-bomber crew climaxed two hours of dramatic action aboard the carrier America and in the air over North Vietnam. It began just 12 minutes after midnight, when the two-man F4 Phantom was downed by enemy fire northwest of Vinh... In less than a minute, radarmen on the missile frigate Jouett had pin-pointed the location of the downed pilots." [Stars & Stripes]

From the Jul 1 Familygram, Captain Hayes' detailed account of the Medal of Honor rescue: "Radarman First Class, Joseph T. WHITTFALL, while on watch in the Combat Information Center of JOUETT, heard the distress call... Under the skillful direction of Radarman First Class Alan R. MELTON, the rescue helicopter and accompanying fixed wing escorts were vectored by radar control through the pitch black night toward the hillside where the survivors were believed to be located." [Familygram]

From the Jul 1 Familygram: "Suddenly, under the canopy of flare illumination, the two survivors splattered with mud, flight suits ripped to shreds, hurtled out of the brush, ran some 20 yards across the clearing, and dove into the waiting helicopter." [Familygram]

From the Jul 1 Familygram: "Then came the report, 'feet wet', which meant they were out over water. Everyone who heard it felt like cheering. The JOUETT, which had been closing the coast at high speed to reduce the length of the flight, now turned on all her aircraft landing lights, and swung into the wind, to receive the helicopter." [Familygram]

quotes: Meanwhile on Market Time — Given's letter, 20 June 1968: Mike's FTG "A" school classmate W.F. "Giv" Given (FTG-3, SN 7942408) wrote from a DER (radar picket escort ship) on Operation Market Time patrol. His ship served as mother ship to 4 Swift boats, carrying ammo, fuel, spare parts, and spare crews: "Once each day, each boat, comes alongside for a spare crew and re-supply." He'd been doing river supply runs and had no laundry or fresh water showers since Taiwan. Turning 20 and celebrating his 1st anniversary, Given was getting orders to USS Tulare (AKA-112) out of San Diego in September — a ship with 6x 3"/50 gun mounts relevant to his FTG rate. He planned to be in Subic July 3–25, then Guam for 5 weeks: "Just think Duc — pretty soon we're half way." [Given's letter to Mike]

quotes: From the Jul 1 Familygram: "On 21 June, JOUETT was paid a great honor and enjoyed a rare privilege when she was visited by three of the most important U.S. Navy Commanders in the Pacific Fleet... He predicted that in years to come they would be happy and proud to know that they had served their nation when it needed them." [Familygram]

Meanwhile in Da Nang — Bill's letter, 21 June 1968: While three admirals were visiting Jouett to congratulate the crew on the Medal of Honor rescue, Bill was on mess duty: "Sounds as if you poor squids had a little action up your way. Just make sure you get those MIG pilots back safe and fuck the others (ha ha.)" He'd seen Bob White from back home, now in the Seabees in Hoi An. Shopping for a Sony 907 tape recorder from an Allied catalog ($34.50) — PX had one for $31 but 3–4 month wait: "So I said fuck that!" Enclosed the $30 he owed Mike. At sea, SAR station. 1800 — MIG-21 DOWNED. Mike's logbook credits the kill to USS Bon Homme Richard. The 1968 Command Operations Report tells it differently — crediting Jouett directly: "Richard TANNER, RD1, one of JOUETT's many expert AIC's (Air Intercept Controller) executed an intercept that resulted in the destruction of one MIG-21." Both are true: CDR Lowell "Moose" Myers (VF-51, F-8H Crusader, Bon Homme Richard) pulled the trigger — maneuvering behind the MiG, firing guns, then destroying it with an AIM-9 Sidewinder — but RD1 Tanner vectored the intercept from Jouett's CIC. Tanner received the Navy Commendation Medal. This was the Navy's 28th MiG kill. 2030 — Refuel from USS Chipola (AO-63).

quotes: Meanwhile in Da Nang — Bill's letter, 13 July 1968: While Mike was at Pearl Harbor 5 days from home, Bill had 226 days left: "You should be back in the states by the time you get this letter you lucky fucker." Bill reacted to Mike's tape about the SAR rescues: "You said in your tape that the chopper got their ass's kicked when they went in land. Boy I bet those chopper guys were really shitting their skivvies when the V.C. started giving them hell." Two red alerts the previous week — rockets hit the air strip and Marble Mountain, 5 miles away. A jeep driver fell asleep at 4 AM and rolled 50 feet down an embankment. "Its been fairly quiet around here the past few nites, but we are expecting to be hit soon." Signed off with dark humor: "I keep you informed if anything big comes up. You know like pulling all the U.S. Troops out or something like that. ha ha!" [Bill's letter to Mike]

quotes: From the Jul 5 Familygram: "It is presently planned that the returning ships of Destroyer Squadron One, JOUETT, PREBLE, and HULL, will arrive in San Diego as a unit... we plan to display the hull number 29 on our helo flight deck as we enter the harbor at Ballast Point. The number 29, formed of crewmembers in white uniforms, when displayed against the grey background of the ship should be visible from the Cabrillo Monument on Point Loma." [Familygram]

quotes: From the Plan of the Day, 18 July 1968: At 0830, a press helicopter took aerial photographs as the crew — in Tropical Whites — formed the number "29" on the flight deck, visible from the Cabrillo Monument on Point Loma. A large sign on the port side read "Happiness is Homecoming." Balloons streamed from the forecastle and fantail. After mooring at Pier 4, refreshments were served on the helo deck and mess decks; dependents and guests were invited aboard for tours. Signed by LCDR J. A. Walker, Jr., Executive Officer. [Plan of the Day]

From the San Diego Union, 19 July 1968 — "Three Warships Return From Vietnam Duty": "The Jouett, with Capt. A. T. Emerson Jr., squadron commander, aboard, wore eight parachutes painted on the superstructure below her bridge, signifying eight aviators were rescued during the deployment." Emerson, of Coronado, had served as commander of the Navy's search and rescue units in the Tonkin Gulf. Capt. Robert S. Hayes reported 932 helicopter takeoffs and landings, 25 night replenishments, and 103 days in the combat zone without a serious accident among his crew of 400. USS Preble (DLG-15) — the ship from which Lassen's Medal of Honor rescue launched — and USS Hull (DD-945) returned alongside. Hull had fired 25,000 five-inch shells, believed to be a record for a single deployment. [San Diego Union]
From the Jul 5 Familygram: "I can assure you that your JOUETTmen are returning home in good health and with a great pride in their achievements." [Familygram]

entries.title: First Letter Home
entries: Mike spent his first days at Treasure Island in classification, physicals, and shots. He picked Long Beach and San Diego for home ports, Hawaii for overseas. With little to do between assignments, he explored San Francisco — ballgames, Chinatown, Fisherman's Wharf, cable cars, movies.
He asked his parents to check with the reserve center about his third-class advancement test results. Temperature in San Francisco: 60s, wearing blues.
quotes: "The plane trip out here was all right but it did seem like a long trip anyway." [Letter]

"There's not much to do around here during the day. Some of the guys get put on working parties but that usually doesn't amount to much. So far I've been able to avoid any of this manual labor!" [Letter]

entries.title: Hippies, Mess Cooking, and the Camera Question
entries: Mike had been on mess cooking duty — 10-hour days on his feet preparing food, but preferred it to cleaning barracks. He reconnected with a buddy from Great Lakes boot camp who spotted Mike's name on a barracks list.
Mike noted the hippies sleeping in parks, painting on sidewalks, holding public speeches, walking around with kittens on strings.
Then the question that would lead to the Super 8 camera and the SAR rescue footage:
He also learned he'd passed the test for third class — *"I was very glad and surprized."*
quotes: "Sunday we went there and spent most of the day. We went to Fisherman's Wharf then went to the Haight/Ashbury section and paid a visit to the 'hippies.' There are a few of them downtown but if you want to see a lot of them you have to go there. I wish I had a camera with me that day." [Letter]

"I think I am going to buy me a movie camera or do you think a still camera would be best. Just in case I do get one, what size projector do we have 8mm or 16mm? I'd like to take a lot of pictures to remember the places I've been and the things I've seen and will be seeing." [Letter]

photos.description: John Brant (2 photos); Plaza and Union Square in downtown San Francisco.

entries.title: The Ship
entries: After three weeks at Treasure Island, Mike received his assignment.
His research:
That weekend, Mike and his Great Lakes buddy crossed the bay to see the carrier USS Enterprise, freshly back from Vietnam:
He was considering buying an Instamatic camera ($14.50 at the Exchange). David's birthday was that day — Mike had mailed a card Saturday. First pay at Treasure Island: $92.00 for twenty days.
quotes: "This morning I was put on assingment. I got the USS JOUETT (DLG-29) out of San Diego. DLG stands for guided missle frigate. I went to the library and found out a little about it." [Letter]
"So, it sounds like a good ship, especially since its not even a year old yet. The living conditions will probably be pretty good." [Letter]
"Its neuclear powered and the biggest ship in the Navy. Let me tell you it is really big. It doesn't seem like your on a ship when you walk around on it." [Letter]

entries.title: Enterprise Arrives in San Diego
entries: While Mike was still at Treasure Island, the *San Diego Union* ran a front-page story on the USS Enterprise (CVN-65) arriving at North Island — the same carrier Mike and his buddy would visit. Page A-2 carried Vietnam War headlines: Buddhist opposition to Thieu, Chinese factional fighting in Canton, and U Thant reporting on Red Bloc aid to Hanoi.

documents.description: Documents: San Diego Union, Sep 17, 1967 — "World's Largest Warship Arrives" (Section B, aerial photo by Joseph Florini); Vietnam War headlines page A-2.

entries.title: Bremerton, Washington
entries: Mike's first letter from the Jouett, typed on USN stationery from the ship in Bremerton.

He was putting in for electronics correspondence courses to fill his evenings and saving money by staying aboard. Sent $80 home for the bank. The ship had gone to sea for weekend exercises — a boiler casualty brought them back early.
Looking ahead to summer 1968 leave — hoping to coordinate with Bill.
quotes: "I like it real well here on the ship. We have some real great guys in our division and the work is not too hard." [Letter]

"I watched part of Wedensday's World Series Game on TV and listened to most of it on the radio today. I think the Cardinals will winx it. At least that's the way Harry Kary figures it will end up so I can't be too wrong." [Letter]

photos.description: USS Jouett alongside another ship; USS Jouett underway; 5" gun mount; MK68 Director.

entries.title: Heading South
entries: Still in Bremerton, preparing to transit to San Diego. The Cardinals won the World Series. Mike had been aboard two weeks and was settling in — eight FTs and eight gunner's mates in his division.

He was chasing his third-class advancement — the reserve center still hadn't entered it in his record. His leading petty officer and the ship's office were writing to the reserve center. Mike sent $50 home for the bank.
Bill sent $5 of the money he owed — *"That came as a surprise to me."*
quotes: "I don't think that things could be much better than what they are here on the ship. The guys in the division are really good to work with and they think that I will have no trouble in getting acquainted with the operation of some of the equipment that we use." [Letter]

entries.title: First Days in San Diego
entries: The Jouett arrived a day early. Mike's first time at sea had been rough:
He was standing watches in the gun director:
The ship was now cruising at Condition III (wartime) watches — four hours on, four or eight off, plus regular work. Departure for WestPac confirmed: **January 16th.**
Seeing the wives and families on the pier when the ship returned from three months away:
quotes: "The first two weekends out I got seasick and the same thing happened last Saturday after we went out. But, I can assure you that I wasn't the only one who did. About 50% of the crew gets sick when we go out." [Letter]
"There are three of us in there and it is like the inside of an Army tank." [Letter]
"I can imagine what it will be like when we get back from the Wes Pac cruise." [Letter]

entries.title: Quick Note
entries: A short letter — Mike wanted his civilian clothes (Levi's permanent press, paisley shirt, black belt, shoes) and the 1968 Allied and Lafayette electronics catalogs sent out. They'd talked on the phone that evening.

entries.title: Halloween
entries: Mike sent home his first roll of film from the ship. A $17 check arrived out of the blue — reimbursement for travel expenses from San Diego to Seattle. He was weighing whether to come home for Christmas.
He needed his "Military Requirements PO 3 and 2" book sent from home — the reserve center had failed to record that he'd completed the course, and he might have to retake the test in February.
quotes: "I guess the one big thing on my mind now is weather to come home for Christmas or not. I'll have to talk to Bill and see what he is going to do then maybe make up my mind." [Letter]

entries.title: Visiting Bill, Escorting the Enterprise
entries: The weekend before, Mike and Bill met up at their aunt Georgia Mae's, and Bill went back to Camp Pendleton on Sunday. That week the Jouett went to sea for a special operation — part of a task force escorting the USS Enterprise during a presidential visit to the West Coast. When the ship came back in on Saturday, Bill was waiting on the pier.

They went to the zoo and Balboa Park. Mike warned Bill about sidewalk photographers in San Diego — *"they are all out to take your money"* — a hustler had already charged Bill $5.25 for a 5×7 black-and-white.
He was taking fire control courses and signing up for electronics correspondence courses that counted for junior college credit ($5 for the first course, the rest free, and you kept the textbooks).
quotes: "Bill was waiting on the pier when we got in. I brought him on the ship and we ate dinner then went into San Diego and spent the rest of the weekend there." [Letter]
"We will be in port for 18 straight days before we go out again. We go out that time then will be here till the middle of January when we leave for West Pac." [Letter]

entries.title: "Sewed the Crow On"
entries: The biggest news: Mike had made third class.
Christmas leave confirmed — starting December 19th, about 14 days. Pay jumped from $65 to $84 per payday.
Danny Wiggins — a friend from back home — was getting married. *"He ought to stay in the Army for another six years, they could really use his kind. ha ha"*
quotes: "If you noticed the return address, I am now third class. I found out last Wed. and sewed the 'crow' on today. I figure I have about $123 in back pay coming... It really feels great. Its like getting your report card and finding out you passed to the next grade. Now, I've got a chance to make second before I get out." [Letter]

"We have one more operation to go out on. This one starts next Monday and lasts for about 5 days. We'll be here in port till the 16 of January when we go on the operation that really counts." [Letter]

entries.title: Last Sea Exercise
entries: The Jouett returned from its final pre-deployment exercise, reaching 90 miles off San Francisco.
Mike's paycheck reflected his new rate: $207, including $143 in back pay. He had reservations on American Airlines for the trip home.
quotes: "Another week at sea and now we are back in port... The next time we go to sea it will be for good." [Letter]

entries.title: The Brothers Meet
entries: Mike picked up his airline tickets and decided to wait at the airport for Bill's flight.

They spent the evening together at the USO before Bill caught the 9:00 bus back to Camp Pendleton. Mike bought Bill a wallet for his birthday — *"He had been using an old one of mine that I let him have when I saw how ragged and beat-up his was."*
Bill owed Mike $45. They stored their civilian clothes together in a locker on the ship.

The Jouett participated in "Blue Lotus," the largest fleet exercise in three years, with 44 ships and Royal Canadian Navy units. The ship celebrated her first birthday on December 3 at sea. [Familygram, 10 Dec 1967]

A Dependents' Cruise was held December 19, with over 100 wives and teenage children aboard. A Christmas party followed — Santa Claus and over 1,000 cookies baked by Jouett's cooks. A 60-foot tree of lights was erected on the foremast. [Familygram, 19 Jan 1968]
Mike flew home to Decatur on American Airlines for two weeks of Christmas leave. He returned to San Diego around January 2, 1968.
quotes: "Sure enough, his plane got in at 4:20 and I met him there." [Letter]

photos.description: Mike in front of Christmas tree; Mike with unknown woman, San Diego; unknown people in front of Christmas tree; unknown woman in front of tree.

entries.title: Jan 4, 1968
entries: Mike saw Bill at Georgia Mae's over the weekend. The ship was undergoing final inspections and loading stores: 11,500 lbs of beef, 800 gallons of milk, 1,600 dozen eggs, and 800 lbs of popcorn. On January 9, Jouett loaded ammunition at Seal Beach Naval Weapons Station. [Familygram, 19 Jan 1968]
quotes: "I am glad I did come home during the holidays. I think it helped my morale a lot and I'll be able to face the months overseas a little better." [Letter]

photos.description: Mike and Bill Ducy together in California — with birthday cake reading "Happy Birthday Mike"; with kids; two posed shots.
Seal Beach, California — 3 photos of the Naval Weapons Station area where Jouett loaded ammunition.

entries.title: Two Days Before Departure
entries: Five days before deployment, Mike served Mass for the chaplain, played the family's tape recording for friends, and prepared his civilian clothes to leave at Georgia Mae's. He was working on an electronics correspondence course — 2 of 25 lessons done.
quotes: "I don't like this job either but all I can do is bear with it. Thats one thing about Navy vs civilian life, if you don't like it you can do something about it but not in this outfit." [Letter]
